items.title: Learning to Stay With Uncertainty
items.abstract: This article reflects on our journey of working to facilitate discussions around the role of Generative AI (GenAI) in education within the Department of Media and Culture Studies (MCW) at Utrecht University during the academic year 2025–2026. What initially appeared to be a manageable question of GenAI’s impact on assessment and writing gradually revealed a complex web of concerns about student engagement, workloads, institutional priorities, and ultimately the purposes and values of higher education itself. Approaching the GenAI moment as a wicked problem, we realized we needed to shift our orientation from finding solutions to creating conditions for collective reflection, imagination, and experimentation. Ultimately, we suggest that responding to GenAI is not so much about finding a way out of uncertainty, but about learning to stay with it by remaining attentive to what emerges, creating space for what might become possible, and continuing to act from the anchor point of the educational purposes and values we care about.

items.title: Legal and Ethical Governance of Artificial Intelligence in Radiology: A Narrative Transcontinental Review Across Pan-Africa, Pan-Asia, and the Americas
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is now embedded in radiology workflows for prioritization, interpretation, quantification, and reporting. As adoption expands, radiologists must address professional responsibility, liability, patient disclosure, data governance, and algorithmic bias. This narrative review used PRISMA-informed, non-systematic methods. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched together with official regulatory and professional websites (including the World Health Organization, the Food and Drug Administration, the Department of Health and Human Services, the National Institute of Standards and Technology, the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, the European Commission, Indian Council of Medical Research, MeitY, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, and AU/AUDA-NEPAD) for English-language literature and legal or policy documents published from January 2018 to March 2026. Search terms combined “radiology,” “artificial intelligence,” “ethics,” “liability,” “privacy,” “bias,” “governance,” “HIPAA,” “GDPR,” “DPDP,” and related terms. Review findings: global principles are converging, but implementation remains regionally contingent. We compare African, Asian, American, and selected international benchmarks, clarify that AFRI-CARE, ASIA-GUIDE, AMERICAS, and RADIANT are proposed conceptual frameworks, and show how they translate shared governance domains into practice. Defensible AI adoption in radiology requires transparent methods, local validation, subgroup monitoring, human oversight, and context-sensitive governance that reflects infrastructure, law, and equity priorities across regions.

items.title: Legal and Regulatory Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Use in Medical and Radiology Research
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical imaging and radiology research, improving image acquisition, interpretation, workflow efficiency, and decision support. However, its rapid adoption has introduced complex legal and regulatory challenges involving patient privacy, data governance, algorithm validation, liability, intellectual property, transparency, cybersecurity, and ethical oversight. A comprehensive understanding of the evolving legal landscape is essential for the safe, effective, and legally compliant implementation of AI in radiology. A narrative review of the published literature and current regulatory guidance was conducted. Relevant international legal and regulatory frameworks governing AI in medical imaging were evaluated, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, General Data Protection Regulation, U.S. Food and Drug Administration guidance on Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, World Health Organization recommendations, International Medical Device Regulators Forum principles, and selected national regulations. Key topics reviewed included data protection, informed consent, AI validation, regulatory approval pathways, post-market surveillance, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, and medico-legal responsibility. Current regulatory frameworks increasingly classify AI-enabled radiology software as SaMD, requiring risk-based evaluation, clinical validation, quality management systems, and continuous post-market performance monitoring. Regulatory authorities emphasize transparency, human oversight, data security, and lifecycle governance of AI systems. Nevertheless, important legal challenges remain, including liability for AI-assisted diagnostic errors, ownership of AI-generated outputs, secondary use of imaging data, cross-border data sharing, algorithmic bias, and regulation of adaptive or continuously learning AI models. The legal framework governing AI in radiology is evolving in parallel with technological innovation. Responsible integration of AI into clinical practice and research requires harmonized international regulations, robust data governance, standardized validation protocols, transparent algorithm development, and clearly defined legal accountability. Continued collaboration among radiologists, researchers, regulators, policymakers, industry, and legal experts will be essential to ensure that AI technologies remain safe, ethical, equitable, and trustworthy while maximizing their potential to improve patient care.

items.title: Legal Education requires Competence in a GenAI World: Why Legal Knowledge is not Enough
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (‘GenAI’) is reshaping what it means to educate competent lawyers. This article devises a Legal Competence Framework based on Le Deist and Winterton’s synthesis of the competence literature augmented by the NSW Solicitor Capability Framework. The Legal Competence Framework delineates the skills students require in their legal education through four interrelated competence dimensions of cognitive competence, functional competence, social competence, and meta-competence. This Framework enables analysis of GenAI’s impact on legal education and assessment. Law is among the most heavily regulated fields of tertiary education and the article seeks to disentangle the complex obligations imposed by the Priestley 11, the Higher Education Standards Framework, the Australian Qualifications Framework and the Threshold Learning Outcomes through applying the Legal Competence Framework. The analysis considers GenAI’s disruption of each learning framework and the impact on learning and assessment, including how GenAI increases the need for social and meta competence. The article explores how GenAI severs the link between traditional unsupervised assessment output and genuine competence discouraging the effortful struggle through which competence develops. It concludes that, whilst supervised assessment remains critical, unsupervised assessment is also essential but its design must shift to focus on assessing learning process rather than output.

items.title: Leveraging AI for Mastery Grading in Large-Enrollment General Chemistry
items.abstract: This chapter details the development and implementation of a mastery learning model for large-enrollment general chemistry. We utilized generative AI and undergraduate research students to refine extensive problem banks and deploy them within the learning management system. This infrastructure enabled a “second-chance” testing framework, which we augmented with instructional resources suited to asynchronous content delivery. These asynchronous content-delivery resources are crucial for providing students with the materials they need for review between successive exam attempts. The instructional resources were selected based on learning design principles explored through our Rethinking Instructional Design for Learning Engagement (RIDLE) faculty learning community. The impact of the mastery learning model was assessed in a study involving more than 500 general chemistry students. We found that combining second-chance testing with an interactive chemistry courseware platform improved student performance on a common midterm exam by approximately two letter grades. Furthermore, student reflections indicate that the mastery learning environment reduces anxiety, fosters a growth mindset, and has a lasting impact on students’ approach to learning.

items.title: Liver Function Assessment in Oncology: Current Tools for Evaluating Hepatic Reserve and Surgical Decision-Making
items.abstract: Accurate assessment of hepatic functional reserve is essential in patients with primary or secondary liver malignancies undergoing liver resection, particularly in the presence of chronic liver disease, chemotherapy-associated liver injury, cholestasis, or portal hypertension. Conventional laboratory parameters and clinical scores, including Child-Pugh, MELD, ALBI, and the combined APRI/ALBI score, provide accessible measures of global hepatic status and risk stratification but do not directly quantify regional function or dynamic metabolic capacity. Complementary approaches include indocyanine green clearance, LiMAx testing, liver stiffness measurement, hepatobiliary scintigraphy, gadoxetic acid-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, and CT/MRI-based future liver remnant volumetry. This narrative review critically examines the strengths, limitations, and clinical applicability of these modalities in the context of contemporary evidence and recommendations. Building on, but extending beyond, the 2023 E-AHPBA-ESSO-ESSR Innsbruck consensus, we incorporate subsequent comparative evidence on blood-based scores and functional imaging and discuss emerging approaches including longitudinal assessment, radiomics, and artificial intelligence. Current evidence supports an individualized, multimodal strategy in which volumetry remains central to surgical planning, while additional functional and portal-hypertension assessment is selected according to the extent of resection, underlying parenchymal disease, previous treatment, and local expertise. No single modality or fixed combination can currently be considered universally superior, highlighting the need for prospective validation of integrated and cost-effective assessment strategies.

items.title: LLM-Based Weak Annotation for Cybersecurity Tweet Classification: A Teacher-Student Framework
items.abstract: Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) relies on the timely identification of emerging threats, enabling organizations and security analysts to support situational awareness and decision-making. Social media platforms such as X (formerly Twitter) have become valuable CTI sources because vulnerabilities and attack activities are often discussed there before appearing in formal reports. However, the rapid growth of cybersecurity discussions on social media has created more content than domain experts can realistically review and annotate, making labeled data a major bottleneck for developing supervised learning approaches. While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise as weak annotators in other domains, their effectiveness for cybersecurity tweet classification and downstream training of domain-specific pre-trained language models (PLMs) remains underexplored. To address this challenge, we propose a Teacher-Student weak supervision framework in which a selected LLM serves as a Teacher to generate weak labels for unlabeled cybersecurity tweets, enabling the training of cybersecurity-specific PLMs without large-scale manual annotation. Experimental results show that PLMs trained solely on LLM-generated labels consistently achieve F1 scores above 0.92, remaining within 3 percentage points of fully human-supervised models across all evaluated architectures. These findings suggest that LLM-based weak annotation offers a practical alternative for constructing cybersecurity-specific training data when expert annotation resources are limited.

items.title: Long Noncoding RNA: An Uncharted Territory in Plant Diseases and Immunity
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are a class of transcripts longer than 200 nucleotides with little or no protein‐coding capacity. They represent a substantial fraction of eukaryotic genomes and function as molecular architects that coordinate diverse biological processes and physiological plasticity, including multilayered plant defence systems, through versatile regulatory interactions at multiple levels of gene regulation. Recent advances in high‐throughput RNA sequencing technologies have greatly expanded the identification of plant lncRNAs, revealing their diverse roles as scaffolds, decoys, guides, and regulatory molecules. These lncRNAs are increasingly recognised as integral components of plant immune systems, contributing critically to host defence mechanisms. This review highlights recent progress in lncRNA identification using computational pipelines as well as emerging artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) based approaches. We further explore current insights into the regulatory functions of lncRNAs during host–pathogen interactions. Notably, we discuss a paradigm‐shifting discovery in lncRNA biology, the finding that many lncRNAs, once presumed to be non‐coding, contain small open reading frames (sORFs) that encode functional micropeptides. Modern predictive modelling has been crucial to identify these sORFs and their peptide products and to show that lncRNAs have multiple functions as regulatory transcripts and peptide precursors in plant immunity.

items.title: Love as a foundation for global citizenship in human-centred AI-driven higher education institutions – a theoretical exploration
items.abstract: Purpose This article aims at exploring global citizenship in the context of higher education institutions (HEIs) which are increasingly affected by artificial intelligence (AI)-driven interactions. By using AI in a human-centred way, educators can expand ways to create global citizenship, offer personalised and empathetic learning while transcending conventional boundaries of education. AI technologies, including natural language processing, machine translation and adaptive learning systems, enable learners to engage with diverse linguistic and cultural materials in increasingly meaningful ways. These tools facilitate immersive language learning, simulate intercultural interactions and provide real-time feedback connected to individual needs in contemporary HEIs. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a theoretical/conceptual approach. Findings While human-centred AI-driven HEIs are gaining importance, the need to create awareness of character strengths and human-centred new learning environments increases as well. In this article, it is argued that pedagogical love, as a character strength, becomes more important in contemporary HEIs than ever before. By integrating AI thoughtfully and ethically into curricula, educators and institutions can contribute to the education of empathetic, multilingual global citizens. Research limitations/implications This research is limited to a qualitative theoretical and conceptual study and may build the base for future empirical studies. Practical implications Love, as a character strength, might support mental health, well-being and human interconnectedness. Originality/value This approach can strengthen the role of HEIs in creating a more peaceful, integrated world.

items.title: Machine-Learning-Enabled Design of Lab-Scale Continuous Distillation Systems for Pharmaceutical Process Development
items.abstract: Abstract Predictive tools for continuous distillation design lag behind upstream pharmaceutical synthesis─including AI-enabled digital tooling for retrosynthetic route design─leaving column specification dependent on computationally expensive simulation or extensive experimentation. This work presents a machine-learning surrogate framework trained entirely on first-principles mechanistic simulations, requiring no experimental distillation data, and eliminating the need for commercial tools such as ChemCad or AspenPlus. Three surrogate models for binary tert-butylamine/alcohol systems (methanol, ethanol, isopropanol) predict distillate and bottoms compositions with mean absolute errors below 0.005 mol/mol and R2 > 0.999, completing a single prediction in under 1 ms─a 24-fold speedup. A coupled Pareto optimizer returns capital-versus-operating-cost trade-off curves in under 10 s, with over 93% of designs verified within ±0.010 mol/mol. Applied to a pharmaceutical case study, the framework correctly identifies isopropanol as the optimal solvent without prior thermodynamic knowledge. The system-agnostic architecture could readily integrate with open-source large language model platforms to further lower the barrier to implementation.

items.title: MANAGEMENT OF ORGANIZATIONAL MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITALIZATION: AN INTEGRATED APPROACH
items.abstract: The article examines an integrated approach to managing organizational marketing communications under digital transformation. It substantiates that digitalization changes traditional communication models, expands stakeholder interaction channels, and increases the need to combine analytical and generative tools. The purpose of the study is to analyze the theoretical foundations and practical aspects of integrated marketing communication management in public administration bodies and nonprofit organizations, including sports organizations. The study analyzes Big Data, CRM systems, social media, AI-generated content, and chatbots in communication activities. The study compares objectives, audiences, channels, digital tools, challenges, and ethical risks. The components of an integrated approach are proposed: consistency of information messages, multichannel communication, orientation toward target audience needs, and continuous feedback. It is established that CRM systems support stakeholder relationship management, personalized interaction, and communication performance analysis; Big Data expands opportunities for audience segmentation and behavioral analysis; and generative artificial intelligence facilitates adaptive content creation and communication automation. Digital integration increases audience trust and engagement, optimizes expenditures, and enables faster responses to environmental changes. The effectiveness of integrated communications depends on the consistency of messages across different channels and their adaptation to the specific needs of stakeholder groups. The systematic combination of digital technologies with traditional communication tools is substantiated as a basis for organizational resilience in a dynamic environment. Ethical, reputational, institutional, and resource-related challenges associated with disinformation, non-transparent use of AI, personal data protection, unequal digital skills, and limited resources are systematized. The scientific novelty lies in conceptualizing an integrated approach as a universal yet sector-differentiated model for managing organizational marketing communications. The practical value lies in applying the model to improve communication strategies.

items.title: Managing Vector Data for Retrieval Augmented Generation@Dagstuhl Seminar Summary
items.abstract: This report summarizes discussions that took place in the context of a Dagstuhl seminar1 to explore the emerging paradigm of AI-native databases designed to support agentic workflows and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with robust database abstractions. The central synthesis of the Dagstuhl discussions is the necessary evolution of databases from passive vector stores into active data-native agentic harnesses that orchestrate AI reasoning and task-centric execution. A recurring lesson across keynotes and working groups is that achieving mission-critical reliability requires integrating AI primitives, such as embeddings, model inference, and semantic operators, as first-class citizens while maintaining traditional database guarantees like transactional consistency, explainability, and cost-aware optimization. This transition necessitates a structured approach to agent memory (spanning episodic, semantic, and procedural scales) and a shift toward adaptive, iterative execution models that go beyond static query planning to accommodate the stochastic nature of foundation models. There is a community consensus that reliability, responsibility, and security (specifically addressing compositional leakage) must be treated as end-to-end concerns supported by holistic benchmarks that evaluate the entire quality chain from retrieval to autonomous action.

items.title: Mapping generative AI in higher education teaching and learning: a scoping review
items.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has rapidly entered higher education, but empirical research on its roles in teaching and learning remains fragmented across instructional activities, outcomes, assessment approaches, and stakeholder perspectives. This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines to map 394 empirical studies of GenAI use in higher education published from November 2022 through December 2025. The review examined how GenAI tools were integrated into authentic teaching and learning activities, what outcomes or skills were targeted, how studies assessed those outcomes, and how students and instructors perceived GenAI use. Across the reviewed studies, GenAI was most often used to support existing academic tasks, especially feedback, tutoring, and writing. The most frequently targeted outcomes included engagement, usability and acceptance, critical thinking, disciplinary knowledge, academic performance, writing quality, and AI literacy. Self-regulated learning, ethics, creativity, feedback quality, and equity received less attention. Assessment practices relied mainly on surveys, tests or rubrics, artifact analysis, and interviews, suggesting that much of the evidence base is shaped by short-term and readily implemented methods. Student and instructor perceptions were predominantly mixed, reflecting perceived benefits alongside concerns about pedagogy, integrity, workload, and governance. The review highlights the need for stronger alignment between learning constructs and assessment methods, more process-sensitive evidence, clearer reporting of governance practices, and greater attention to equity in GenAI-supported higher education.

items.title: Mapping of Textile Waste Management Techniques and Conversion Pathways: A Bibliometric Review
items.abstract: The global textile industry generates waste at multiple stages, including fiber production, fabric manufacturing, chemical processing, garment production, finishing, and post-consumption. This study examines approaches for effective textile waste management and maps them across stages of activity. It includes two components: a bibliometric trend analysis and a review of developments, practices, and strategies in textile waste management and valorization. The review identifies 2749 research articles and 988 distinct keywords, highlighting themes such as recycling, value-added products, circular economy, and sustainability. The study maps in-process, after-process, and post-consumer waste within the supply chain or redirects it into value-added products within a circular economy framework. In some cases, textile waste is reused in production through reduction, reuse, and repurposing without recycling. Recent research focuses on converting natural and synthetic textile waste such as fibers, yarns, fabrics, trims, and dyes into outputs including recycled fibers and fabrics, nonwovens, lactic acid, glucose, ethanol, biogas, char, and compost. Mechanical recycling is gaining importance for post-industrial waste. When reuse or mechanical recycling is not feasible, chemical and biological treatments are applied. Advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning support efficient sorting, waste prediction, and recycling processes.

items.title: Mapping Road Safety Inequity in India Using Artificial Intelligence Where Fatalities Cluster, Where AI Road-Safety Technology Is Deployed, and What Should Be Prioritised
items.abstract: India records more road deaths than any other country in the world, with 172,890 in 2023, but the public data behind that number is rarely studied to ask whether the danger is spread evenly and whether new artificial-intelligence road-safety technology is reaching the worst impacted areas. This paper uses official Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) figures for the country, for every state and union territory, and for fifty cities, together with a list of few of India’s AI road-safety deployments, to map where road deaths cluster and to compare that with where the technology has already been installed. Then, it builds a simple, literature-based model of how many lives the proven tools could theoretically save. The work is quantitative, with fifteen figures and six tables. The main results are as follows. The absolute and per-person data are almost unrelated, with a correlation of only 0.28, so Uttar Pradesh has the most deaths but only an average rate per person, while Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh, and Telangana have the highest rates per person. AI systems have mostly been implemented in states that already had strong administration rather than to the worst impacted ones, which matches the World Bank’s split between high-capacity and low-capacity states. A preventable-fraction model estimates that AI-suited vehicle and enforcement measures could prevent roughly 26,000 deaths a year at moderate coverage, in a range of 11,900 to 49,500, with automated speed enforcement the largest single measure at 17,600. Even the high estimate is below the national target of halving deaths by 2030, so road engineering and emergency care must take over the burden of covering the rest. Most of the preventable deaths fall in the worst impacted states that currently have no major deployment, which shows the real cost of the deployment gap.

items.title: Maritime transport and policy research over the past 50 years: a review across four maritime journals
items.abstract: Journal focused bibliometric studies, especially those examining leading or highly relevant journals, are widely acknowledged as an effective way to capture the intellectual structure of a field. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of four important journals which have strong orientation in maritime transport and policy field using R-Bibliometrix package and VOSviewer. The final dataset consists of 2,889 articles published between 1976 and 2024. The results mapped the intellectual research landscape of the field by identifying leading authors, institutions, regions, influential articles, and major research clusters. Keyword co-occurrence analysis shows that the most frequently discussed topics include ports operations, logistics, container shipping, maritime safety, and climate change adaptation. The field also engages with promising areas of human-centred issues such as seafarer, maritime education and training, human factors, human error and non-technical skills. The findings show an interesting direction that integrates economic and technical operations with human and societal dimensions. Additionally, the findings potentially provide insights for researchers and practitioners seeking collaborations or directions, and policymakers seeking priorities in the maritime transport and policy domain.

items.title: Marketing misinformation in the age of AI
items.abstract: Abstract We shine a spotlight on marketing misinformation—claims about products and brands that contradict or distort verifiable facts. Misinformation may be created unintentionally or intentionally by companies, competitors, customers, or third parties seeking to harm companies or consumers. We focus on the role of AI in creating, obfuscating, and disseminating misinformation in the form of text, audio, images, and videos generated using large language models. This type of information can pose a substantial risk for brand safety. Consumers may be aware that AI can generate misinformation but may lack the ability to guard against it. We discuss how different stakeholders in the information ecosystem can help in the prevention and correction of misinformation and propose a future research agenda in this critical and fast‐growing area.

items.title: Materials foundation models fail together: Correlated errors and collective blind spots
items.abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) are increasingly combined to screen candidate crystals, but the reliability gains from consensus and disagreement depend on diversity among model errors. We quantify error dependence across 15 public uMLIPs using density functional theory (DFT) convex-hull distances for 248,623 structures from the Wang–Botti–Marques benchmark. The mean pairwise error correlation is 0.39, corresponding to 4.3 effective models. Because rank-1 removal cannot distinguish shared model bias from shared reference effects, we applied two additive-reference controls; correlations remained 0.44 and 0.42, with effective model counts of 3.7 and 3.9. A stratified permutation null that preserves each model’s coupling to the DFT reference while destroying cross-model correlation showed that false discoveries shared by single-model, consensus, and agreement-based screening occurred 141 times more often than expected ( p < 0.001 ). Agreement-gated screening admitted 1620 false discoveries versus 7 under the null. The median consensus did not outperform the best individual model and produced a 27.6% false-discovery rate among predicted-stable structures. Cross-model disagreement was nearly uninformative (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC, 0.51), whereas the consensus margin reached AUC 0.75 and conformal-normalized margin 0.85; standard split-conformal intervals reached 0.68. Removing the 30% of candidates closest to the threshold reduced the retained false-discovery rate to 17.8%, but was exactly equivalent to tightening the stability threshold at matched shortlist size. These results show that correlated errors can limit ensemble reliability and that threshold-aware scores provide a practical ranking of screening risk. We release a reproducible reliability atlas and benchmark.

items.title: Measuring a scaffold from inside: an operator-authored self-measurement harness for a constitutional runtime over a hosted language model
items.abstract: Interactive intelligent systems constructed over hosted large language models cannot retrain the substrate on which they depend, and so their designers enforce a named epistemology at the surrounding scaffold layer. A difficulty follows that has received little methodological attention: when quality regresses, the regression frequently belongs to the scaffold rather than the substrate, and identifying it requires instruments that measure the scaffold itself rather than the model beneath it. This article reports one such instrument set, added to a live constitutional runtime between 17 and 18 July 2026 and extended with a production drift observer on 19 August 2026, and situates it as a reusable design pattern. The layer comprises six components—operator-authored adversarial batteries held as versioned regression fixtures, deterministic pattern screens encoding named defects, an emission quarantine that retains failure evidence as a first-class object, an instrument-health monitor issuing autonomous handoffs, continuous-integration delivery tripwires, and an observe-only production drift detector that accumulates a hand-labelling corpus from live traffic without altering any replies. Eight falsifiable harness predictions are stated (H1 through H8), each named against a specific runtime carrier—a code path, a database table, or a typed field—and each paired with an explicit falsification condition; their relationship to the eight pre-registered outcome predictions (F1 through F8) of a companion architecture paper is stated in a dedicated reconciliation section, since the harness reported here is the instrument set on which those outcome predictions depend. Of the eight, five (H1, H2, H3, H5, H7) carry dated on-platform observations and are reported in a dedicated observed subsection; three (H4, H6, H8) are prospective—predictions about experiments that have not yet occurred—and are reported separately under that label, so that no reader mistakes the distribution of evidence. The predictions are offered for adversarial replication under an honest empirical frame rather than as settled results: the batteries were authored by the platform’s operator, classification is not independent, and the number of platforms studied is one. The discussion states a narrow priority claim, distinguishes the enforcement point of composition-time assertion from adjacent techniques, extends the pattern to the governance of learning loops—a scaffold that adapts must be measured by the same discipline that measures a scaffold that enforces—and argues that the interaction properties a reader encounters, an observation lock and per-turn provenance grounding, become testable precisely because they are structurally enforced.

items.title: Measuring Creativity as a Gateway to Innovation
items.abstract: Measuring creativity has always felt like wandering down a cul-de-sac: Everyone agrees it’s important, yet their attempts to pin it down often lead nowhere. Traditional tests - like counting how many new uses someone can dream up for a paper clip - capture flashes of cleverness but say little about whether those ideas would actually work in the messy real world. Over the decades, researchers from Terman to Torrance to Martinsen have wrestled with the problem, but measurements of creativity have had a way of slipping through their fingers. The OECD’s PISA 2022 framework tried to shrug off some of these limitations by adding new dimensions such as written expression, visual expression, and scientific problem-solving. The first wave of results in 2023 not only looked promising but also revealed fresh complications: Students could generate copious ideas, but scoring them fairly remained a challenge. Some responses were brilliant, and others seemed like abject failures, but even the failures sometimes contained a spark of originality that defied conventional rubrics. Now, with generative AI reshaping how we think, learn, and create, the task is shifting again. Future assessments like PISA 2029’s Media & AI Literacy module may finally begin to capture aspects of creativity once overlooked, from digital storytelling to collaborative problem-solving in human-machine teams. The broader lesson is clear: Measuring creativity is not about designing one flawless test but about accepting human frailties, staying flexible, and continuously adapting our definitions and evaluations of imagination as new tools and contexts emerge.

items.title: MechaScreener: Large language model-based automated screening for systematic reviews and research
items.abstract: Systematic reviews are the gold standard for evidence synthesis, but the manual title and abstract screening of thousands of references creates a severe bottleneck. Existing automated tools have historically struggled to achieve the near-perfect recall (sensitivity) required for reliable reviews. We developed MechaScreener as a 'zero-shot' automated screening tool that utilises a large language model to rank article relevance. The tool requires no initial training data or manual pre-screening, as MechaScreener directly applies user-provided question elements (PICO) or inclusion/exclusion criteria to assign an ordinal relevance score (1-5) to each reference. We evaluated the tool in two phases: a development phase using five reference libraries to optimise prompts, and an independent evaluation phase using 10 diverse Cochrane review libraries (comprising both randomised controlled trials [RCTs] and non-RCTs) containing over 58,000 references. In the evaluation dataset, MechaScreener achieved a perfect recall of 1.00 (100%) in all 10 reviews, ensuring that no relevant articles were missed (pooled record-level 95% CI: 0.98-1.00). Concurrently, it achieved an overall macro-average specificity of 0.61 (61%, cluster bootstrap 95% CI: 0.46-0.75; pooled record-level specificity 0.59, 95% CI: 0.59-0.60). Specificity varied from 0.21 in broad public health topics to 0.91 in precise pharmacological interventions, reflecting the tool's built-in conservatism when evaluating ambiguous abstracts. By safely eliminating over 60% of irrelevant literature during the initial screening phase without compromising recall, MechaScreener functions as a highly reliable but low-effort 'first-pass' filter, allowing researchers to substantially reduce manual workloads and reallocate resources towards full-text review and data extraction.

items.abstract: The overall research question asks to what extent the dynamics of self-regulated learning and the immersive experience predict the transfer of aprocedural skill from virtual reality to the physical world. items.title: Metaheuristic optimized and explainable machine learning for predicting the compressive strength of lightweight foamed concrete
items.abstract: Abstract Lightweight foamed concrete (LFC) can provide reduced structural dead load and enhanced thermal performance, however the compressive strength of LFC is determined by the complex nonlinear interactions between the mixture constituents, density and testing age, which makes the prediction and proportioning of the product difficult. This study addresses this challenge through leakage-resistant machine learning combined with metaheuristic optimization and explainable artificial intelligence. A literature-derived database of 993 observations was divided by mix-design group into 795 development records representing 276 groups and 198 unseen-test records representing 69 independent groups, with no overlap. Random forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) models, together with their Leopard Seal Optimizer (LSO), Harris Hawks Optimizer (HHO), and Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA) optimized variants, were assessed using 10-fold grouped cross-validation and a completely held-out test set. SHAP and PDP-ICE analyses were subsequently applied to the best-generalizing model. LSO-XGB achieved the strongest grouped out-of-fold performance ((R 2 = 0.888); RMSE = 3.93 MPa), whereas HHO-XGB performed best on unseen data ((R 2 = 0.875); RMSE = 4.10 MPa), reducing the baseline-XGB RMSE by 4.1%. HHO-XGB also produced a median absolute error of 0.82 MPa, with 95.96% and 97.47% of predictions within 5 and 10 MPa, respectively. items.title: Moderate exosuit use reduces the incidence of back discomfort in logistic warehouse workers: a randomised controlled trial with an exploratory dose-stratified analysis
items.abstract: Evidence on whether exosuits reduce workplace injuries is mixed. We studied whether exosuits can reduce back discomfort among warehouse workers. Ninety-seven participants were randomised to a control or exosuit group; for exploratory analysis, exosuit participants were stratified as moderate or low users. Surveys at baseline and four follow-ups assessed workplace discomfort, perceived back effort, usability, and adverse events. Intention-to-treat analysis showed that exosuit users had no difference in back discomfort intensity and incidence than the control group. However, exosuit users did have reductions in overall body discomfort. Exploratory analyses showed that moderate users had a 2–3-fold lower incidence of back discomfort than the control group, with 20% reductions in perceived back effort and no increased discomfort at other joints. Consistent exosuit use reduced the likelihood of experiencing low back discomfort. However, disparity between intention-to-treat and dose-stratified analyses suggests effectiveness is dose- and job-fit-dependent, supporting targeted implementation. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05802914.

items.title: Modern Techniques in Computer Vision
items.abstract: Computer vision enables computer systems to extract useful meaning from images and video. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, have improved the ability of machines to recognise objects, interpret scenes, and identify visual patterns. This paper presents a structured review of AI techniques used in computer vision, with emphasis on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), their main processing stages, practical applications, and continuing limitations. It explains why manually designed visual features can be unreliable when images vary in lighting, scale, viewpoint, or background, and how learned representations help address these problems. Applications in healthcare, transportation, astronomy, and industrial inspection are discussed alongside concerns involving data quality, bias, privacy, explainability, and computational cost. The paper is a conceptual review based on established literature and does not claim a new experiment or measured performance result. It concludes that responsible deployment requires not only accurate models, but also representative data, careful evaluation, human oversight, and monitoring after deployment

items.title: Modernizing Pakistan's trade ecosystem: The role of artificial intelligence in digital customs and trade facilitation
items.abstract: As AI technology evolves, it has opened up new prospects for enhancing customs management and promoting international commerce. Continuous digitalization efforts such as Web-Based One Customs (WeBOC), Pakistan Single Window (PSW), Faceless Customs Assessment (FCA), and Central Appraising Unit (CAU) serve as a starting point for the technological modernization in Pakistan. The present study focuses on how AI can transform the trade landscape in Pakistan, especially in terms of efficiency in digital customs management, trade facilitation, and transparency and compliance. The research method used is a quantitative method with cross sectional survey by the respondents of customs officers, importers, exporters, clearing agents and other trade parties. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) is used to evaluate the proposed relationships using SmartPLS 4. The results revealed that the adoption of AI is statistically significant and positively related to customs operational efficiency, trade facilitation, and transparency and compliance based on simulated data of 250 respondents. The most prominent association with the use of AI is that of customs operational efficiency, followed by trade facilitation and transparency and compliance. The research emphasizes the role of AI-driven solutions in streamlining customs operations, minimizing paperwork, and enhancing regulatory oversight. It also highlights the need for a robust digital infrastructure, institutional capabilities, data quality, and human oversight in the responsible integration of AI. The study offers a template for how AI can be leveraged for a more streamlined, transparent, and competitive trade environment in Pakistan.

items.title: Momentum, Commentary Tone, and Earnings Surprise in LLM Financial Forecasts
items.abstract: Which inputs drive a language model's financial forecast? We construct synthetic earnings announcements that independently reverse 20-day momentum, non-informational commentary tone, and whether fixed actual EPS beats a manipulated consensus. Six instruction/chat checkpoint conversions from four families (0.49-7.61B base parameters) receive 2,016 prompts each under a direct-answer Q8_0 protocol. The design includes 24 numerical blocks, six commentary pairs, profits and losses, rising and falling annual EPS, and two surprise sizes. Both A/B answer assignments and U/D cover all 384 primary scenarios per conversion. We estimate matched changes in conditional answer-prefix scores, not calibrated market probabilities. Across these checkpoints, the primary EPS contrast ranges from -0.19 to 86.80 percentage points. The magnitude of the primary signed tone contrast exceeds that of EPS in 5 of six models, and momentum exceeds it in 5. Natural-word numerical diagnostic accuracy ranges from 51.0 to 95.8 percent. Answer-encoding, wording, context, and conversion controls qualify these results. The experiment measures observable input reliance and numerical recognition; it establishes neither an internal reasoning mechanism nor realized return predictability. Public benchmark prompts, recorded scores, and an interactive recorded-results explorer accompany the study.

items.title: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the “oxide gatekeeper” in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
items.abstract: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic “gatekeeper,” regulating oxidation through a “breathing mode” of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a “rupture mode” leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.

items.title: Needle-thin: reconstructing on-edge microblade production and contextual integrity through lithic refitting in the Magdalenian of Cova Gran de Santa Linya (SE Pyrenees)
items.abstract: The study of human behaviour in prehistoric societies is a primary objective of archaeological and anthropological research. One way to investigate past behaviour is through the analysis of technological organisation. The resolution at which archaeologists can examine the past is highly dependent on the sedimentary dynamics and site-formation processes that play a key role in the preservation of the archaeological record. To mitigate the limitations inherent in the archaeological record, lithic refitting has emerged as a valuable method to enhance the contextual resolution of Palaeolithic sites. However, this method has not been uniformly applied to assess the impact of syn -postdepositional processes in archaeology. Cova Gran de Santa Linya (NE Iberia) preserves evidence of long-term sedimentary and erosive cycles that have shaped the differential preservation of archaeological evidence. This is exemplified by unit 7P (20.5 k −18 k cal BP), located in the Platform Sector, which has been partially affected by erosive processes within the site, resulting in complex vertical and horizontal stratigraphic relationships within the site’s Last Glacial Maximum sequence. To assess the impact of natural and anthropogenic disturbances on Level 7P, we conducted lithic refitting and technological analysis, combined with spatial data. Refittings indicated the lithic assemblage remained unaffected by erosive events at the site, reinforcing the in situ preservation of the occupation. The spatial distribution revealed a dense cluster of refitted artefacts in 2 m 2 . Refitting within this cluster revealed highly specialised and complex behaviours associated with microblade production. Archaeostratigraphic, spatial, technological and contextual data were combined to assess whether this accumulation is the result of anthropogenic or natural factors. We have also investigated what human activities underlying the formation of lithic clusters. The main cluster of 7P, in conjunction with other elements of the archaeological record facilitates the identification of spatial organisational patterns characterised by short-distance intra-site mobility. Overall, we highlight systematic refitting as valuable holistic approach for enhancing contextual resolution in archaeological assemblages, thereby refining our understanding of the natural and human factors involved in the formation of Palaeolithic sites.

items.title: Negotiating Authorship with Generative AI in Cinema Education: Attribution and Creative Decision-Making in Screenwriting
items.abstract: This study examines how cinema students attribute authorship during AI-assisted screenwriting and how those judgments relate to creative decisions. Drawing on a fourteen-week, design-based course, it compares logbooks with 436 student turns across twenty generative-AI conversations. In four of six co-writing cases, students selected and retained system-originated material. The clearest tension appeared when students claimed the idea as their own but assigned the text entirely to AI while repeatedly rejecting generated material, a response the instrument’s own categories leave ambiguous. Read against Livingston, Gaut and Sellors, these cases show that textual generation, creative decision-making and authorship attribution can diverge within one process. Cinema education should ask not only who authored a text, but on what basis.

items.title: Neuromorphic Computing and Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) for Ultra-Low-Power Edge Intelligence: Architectures, Learning Paradigms, and Silicon Benchmarks
items.abstract: Abstract—The continuous scaling of conventional Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) on classical Von Neumann architectures has reached severe physical boundaries governed by the 'memory wall' and unsustainable thermal dissipation. Battery-constrained edge computing environments—including autonomous micro-robotics, bio-implantable telemetry, and space-borne remote sensing—demand continuous, milliwatt-scale machine perception that standard GPUs and digital tensor accelerators cannot deliver. Neuromorphic Computing and Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) establish an alternative non-Von Neumann computing paradigm inspired by biological neurobiology, processing information via sparse, event-driven temporal spikes rather than dense, continuous matrix multiplications. However, deploying high-performance SNNs across resource-constrained edge hardware introduces profound foundational challenges: non-differentiable threshold activation dynamics that complicate gradient-based training, temporal latency vs. spike sparsity trade-offs, and microarchitectural fragmentation across asynchronous neuromorphic silicon. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of neuromorphic computing for ultra-low-power edge intelligence. We formalize the non-linear differential dynamics of Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) and Adaptive Exponential (AdEx) neuron models, derive the mathematical formulations of surrogate gradient backpropagation through time (BPTT), and analyze ANN-to-SNN rate-conversion bounds. Furthermore, we construct an empirical hardware testbed benchmarking neuromorphic silicon platforms (Intel Loihi 2 and SynSense Speck) against state-of-the-art edge accelerators (NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and Google Coral Edge TPU) across neuromorphic vision (DVS-Gesture, N-MNIST) and real-time edge bio-signal classification (MIT-BIH Arrhythmia). Our experimental findings demonstrate that event-driven SNN execution on neuromorphic silicon achieves up to a 42.6x reduction in dynamic energy consumption over edge GPUs while maintaining competitive classification accuracy (within 0.8% of floating-point DNN baselines) and sub-10ms inference latencies. Finally, we formulate open research directions in memristive in-memory computing crossbars, on-chip continuous spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and hybrid large-scale neuromorphic foundation models.

items.title: O potencial da Inteligência Artificial para a Gestão do Conhecimento na Petrobras
items.abstract: This article discusses the growing importance of knowledge as an organizational asset and the integration between Knowledge Management (KM) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). This integration can enhance KM processes, while consistent KM practices provide high quality data for intelligent algorithms. The purpose of this study is to present how Petrobras is structuring itself to apply AI in its KM processes. This is a case study based on content analysis of documents (internal reports, consulting reports, event materials), interviews with the company’s KM team, and a literature review. The study contributes to the field by highlighting Petrobras’ journey as a complex and regulated organization. This journey involved combining agile methods, experimentation, international scouting, and other strategies to meet business requirements aligned with organizational needs, expanding the benefits of this technology. As a result, in addition to the strong ROI potential and the intangible benefits associated with applying AI to KM processes, the study concludes that this innovation represents a strategic step for Petrobras. items.title: Occupational Characteristics and Ergonomic Assessment of Work Postures among Bamboo and Cane Weaving Craftsmen in Assam, India
items.abstract: Aims: The study aimed to assess the occupational and ergonomic characteristics of selected bamboo and cane weaving craftsmen in Assam, with particular emphasis on workspace sitting arrangements, adopted working postures, and associated ergonomic risk. Study Design: A descriptive research design was adopted. Place and Duration of Study: The study was conducted in the Barpeta Cluster of Assam from June 2024 to July 2025. Methodology: A total of 260 craftsmen were purposively selected (n = 97 bamboo-only, n = 47 cane-only, and n = 116 bamboo-and-cane craftsmen) to assess occupational and personal characteristics. Detailed observational postural assessment and Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) were conducted among a purposively selected subsample of 60 craftsmen (20 participants per activity group; 10 males and 10 females). Data were collected using a structured interview schedule and observational sheets. Associations between posture types and personal variables were examined using the chi-square test of independence and post-hoc residual analysis. Results: The mean age and work experience of the respondents were 42.88 years and 15.42 years, respectively, while the mean daily working duration was 7.48 hours. Overall, 43.46% of craftsmen worked for 6–8 hours per day and 39.23% worked for more than 8 hours. A wooden low stool/Pidha was the most commonly reported sitting arrangement during splitting (57.70%), stripping (42.30%), bending (53.80%), weaving (38.50%), and finishing (46.20%). Among the 60 craftsmen assessed through REBA, squatting, crossed-leg sitting, one-leg-folded/one-leg-extended sitting, and sitting upright were observed across different activities. High REBA risk was particularly pronounced during bending, where 100% of the observed respondents across the reported gender and craft groups were classified in the high-risk category for both body sides. During splitting, stripping, weaving, and finishing, high-risk classifications were also frequently observed, particularly among squatting, crossed-leg, and one-leg-folded/one-leg-extended postures. A statistically significant association was found between age and type of adopted posture (χ² = 14.56, p = 0.006), whereas associations with gender (χ² = 5.34, p = 0.069) and work experience (χ² = 9.81, p = 0.279) were not significant. Post-hoc analysis showed that squatting was adopted significantly more frequently than expected among craftsmen aged 20–35 years (adjusted residual = +2.34, p < 0.05). Conclusion: Bamboo and cane weaving involve prolonged daily work, predominantly low-level sitting arrangements, constrained postures, and considerable ergonomic risk. The high prevalence of high-risk REBA classifications, particularly during bending, highlights the need for ergonomically appropriate sitting arrangements and workstation design. Incorporating suitable seating, posture modification, adequate rest pauses, task variation, and ergonomic awareness may help reduce postural strain and occupational discomfort and improve the safety and efficiency of traditional bamboo and cane weaving work.

items.title: Occupational Demands and Workplace Resources Among Pediatric Hospital Staff During a Health System Crisis
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: The psychosocial and organizational demands of healthcare work intensify during public health crises, with implications for professional functioning. This study aimed to identify the occupational demands and workplace resources associated with professional functioning among pediatric hospital staff, using the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) framework as the guiding theoretical model. Methods: A cross-sectional, mixed-methods study was conducted among 903 employees of a pediatric emergency hospital in 2024, using a custom questionnaire and thematic analysis of open-ended responses, interpreted through the JD-R framework. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed five occupational functioning outcomes, with workload, age, sex, tenure, occupational category, COVID-sector work, and relocation as predictors. Results: A significant workload increase was the most consistent predictor, associated with four of the five outcomes (aOR 2.04–7.16), and relocation was associated with three outcomes (aOR 1.70–2.49); COVID-sector assignment was not independently associated with the other four outcomes after correction for multiple testing, but was associated with lower odds of difficulty returning to work among infected staff (aOR 0.38). Thematic analysis identified seven themes aligned with the JD-R framework; most were significantly more frequent among COVID-sector staff after FDR correction, although a sensitivity analysis restricted to respondents who answered the open-ended item attenuated this pattern for several themes and reversed it for one. Quantitative–qualitative comparisons showed convergent associations across the constructs examined. Conclusions: Workload and organizational disruption were more consistently associated with impaired occupational functioning than formal sector assignment. These findings support the value of monitoring psychosocial workload indicators in occupational health surveillance and highlight team-level resources as a relevant direction for future prevention efforts.

items.title: Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems and ISO 45001: A Bibliometric Analysis
items.abstract: Introduction: Occupational health and safety (OHS) is governed by mandatory national regulations, whereas ISO 45001, the international standard for OHS management systems (OHSMS), is adopted voluntarily; yet the scientific literature on OHSMS remains insufficiently mapped. This study analyzed the scientific output and academic impact of research on OHSMS and ISO 45001 between 2018 and 2026. Method: A descriptive bibliometric study was conducted, adapted from PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. Scopus was searched using ("Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems" AND "ISO 45001") up to 24 August 2026; of 496 records identified, 350 documents were analyzed with Python and Bibliometrix. Results: Articles represented 64.9% of documents and 87.7% were in English. Annual output rose from 16 documents in 2018 to 67 in 2025; Indonesia, Portugal, and the Russian Federation were the most productive countries. Engineering predominated (40.6%), and 70% of documents reported no funding. Management systems and risk assessment were the main thematic axes, while safety culture, certification, and artificial intelligence appeared in the most recent period. Impact was moderate (7.36 citations per document; maximum author h-index = 5 within the corpus); the most cited document received 89 citations, and Safety Science (h-index = 9) was the most influential journal. Collaboration networks were fragmented. Conclusions: Research on OHSMS and ISO 45001 is growing but shows moderate academic impact and weak articulation of international collaboration. Practical Applications: Findings can help researchers and funders prioritize collaborative, funded studies on ISO 45001 implementation and the empirical evaluation of emerging digital and artificial intelligence applications.

items.title: Occupational risk factors for abdominal wall hernias among working-age adults in Saudi Arabia: A cross-sectional analysis of national health survey and labor force data
items.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND: Occupational exposures involving heavy manual lifting, prolonged standing, and physically demanding labor represent established risk factors for abdominal wall hernia development. Saudi Arabia’s labor force, characterized by a substantial manual workforce concentrated in construction, manufacturing, and agriculture, may carry elevated occupational hernia risk, yet population-level analyses quantifying these associations are absent from the literature. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to characterize the prevalence of self-reported abdominal wall hernias by occupational category among Saudi working-age adults, quantify the association between specific occupational exposures and hernia risk, and assess geographic and demographic variations in occupationally attributed hernia burden. METHODS: This cross-sectional descriptive study analyzed secondary data from the Saudi Health Interview Survey 2018 ( n = 10,735 adults aged 18–65 years), Saudi General Authority for Statistics Labor Force Survey 2018–2023, and Saudi Ministry of Health Annual Statistical Yearbooks. Hernia prevalence was stratified by occupational category using the International Standard Classification of Occupations. The specific exposures analyzed included heavy manual lifting, prolonged standing, and physically demanding labor. Comparative analyses and prevalence ratios (PRs) were calculated. Reporting followed strengthening the reporting of observational studies in epidemiology guidelines. RESULTS: The overall self-reported hernia prevalence was 8.3% among working-age adults. Manual laborers demonstrated the highest hernia prevalence (14.7%), followed by construction and extraction workers (13.2%) and agricultural workers (11.8%), compared to 4.1% among professional/managerial workers. Hernia prevalence was significantly associated with daily heavy lifting exceeding 20 kg (PR: 2.84; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.31–3.49), prolonged standing exceeding 6 h per day (PR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.42–2.18), and duration of occupational exposure exceeding 10 years (PR: 2.21; 95% CI: 1.87–2.61). Male sex, age 45–65 years, and concurrent obesity amplified occupational hernia risk. Geographic analysis revealed highest hernia procedure rates in regions with concentrated industrial and agricultural workforces. CONCLUSIONS: Occupational exposures, particularly heavy manual lifting and prolonged standing, are significantly associated with abdominal wall hernia prevalence in Saudi Arabia’s working-age population. Targeted workplace prevention programs, ergonomic interventions, pre-employment screening, and enhanced access to hernia repair services for manual labor sectors represent priority occupational health policy actions.

items.title: OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY RISK ASSESSMENT DURING PURSE SEINE VESSEL UNLOADING OPERATIONS AT KUTARAJA OCEANIC FISHING PORT, ACEH
items.abstract: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is a crucial aspect of preventing workplace accidents and illnesses, particularly during high-risk vessel unloading operations at the Kutaraja Oceanic Fishing Port (OFP) in Banda Aceh. Inadequate implementation of safety programs, such as hazard identification, risk analysis, and risk control, is a primary cause of workplace accidents in this sector. This study aimed to identify activities and analyze occupational safety risks associated with the unloading process of purse seine vessels at OFP Kutaraja over one month, focusing on seven vessels. The methodology involved direct observation, interviews with crew members, and data analysis using the Job Safety Analysis (JSA) approach. Risk assessment was conducted using a risk matrix that factored in both severity and probability. The results indicate that the unloading operation comprises three main stages: pre-unloading, the unloading process, and post-unloading. Each stage presents varying levels of risk, ranging from "Acceptable" to "Unacceptable". The highest risks were associated with handling fish-filled brail nets and transporting the catch, activities that carry the potential for serious accidents. Contributing risk factors included the lack of use of personal protective equipment (PPE), suboptimal work procedures, and unsafe working conditions. Safety during vessel unloading operations could be improved through regular training, increased PPE usage, and the implementation of a JSA-based risk control system.

items.title: Occupational Visual Strain and Associated Ergonomic Risk Factors Among Watchmakers: A Cross-Sectional Study of Binocular Vision, Ocular Pain and Intraocular Pressure
items.abstract: Background: Watch repairing involves prolonged near-vision activity, monocular loupe use, sustained convergence, awkward postures, and repetitive fine motor movements, potentially contributing to ocular strain. The ocular and ergonomic impact of such occupations has not yet been documented. Objective: To study the ocular stress profile along with ergonomics risk factors among male watchmakers from Kolkata, India. Methods: This comparative cross-sectional study included 140 men aged 40–50 years, comprising 70 watchmakers with over 15 years of occupational exposure and 70 controls. Visual pain was assessed using a visual analogue scale (VAS), near point of convergence (NPC) and accommodation using the RAF rule, fusional vergence using a prism bar, ocular movements using a synoptophore, intraocular pressure (IOP) using non-contact tonometry, and visual acuity using a Snellen chart. Fundus photography and ergonomic assessments were also performed. Data were analysed using independent-samples t-tests (SPSS version 26; p<0.05). Results: Watchmakers exhibited significantly greater visual pain (7.29±0.58 cm vs. 3.81±0.30 cm; p<0.001) and receded NPC (16.57±1.51 cm vs. 7.86±1.35 cm; p<0.001), both remaining significant after Holm correction. Adduction was reduced (p=0.010), whereas IOP was higher in both eyes (p=0.044). Visual acuity and anthropometric differences were statistically insignificant. Major ergonomic concerns included inadequate rest periods, monocular loupe use, postural strain, and hand discomfort. Conclusion: Prolonged monocular near work by watchmakers can lead to convergence insufficiency-like symptoms, increased eye pain, and increased intraocular pressure. It is necessary for ergonomic measures such as using bi-ocular devices and proper work rest cycles and eye screenings to be taken.
